reason: The existential actual-MLE counterexample retains the spatial, overlap, interior, homophily and positive asymptotic variance guards and failure of equation (36). It retains the three entered-array square sums, independently checked exactly. It does not identify those arrays with the estimator coefficients or actual variances, and omits W1 numerical certificates, W2-W3 identities, W5 moments/tail constants and the other W6 limit/coverage assertions. The cyclic sequence extends the stated 3K witness to all natural sample sizes; restricting to the 3K subsequence gives the same witness up to translation and indexing. The definitions do not assume the failed expansion.

The asymptotic and finite components together state clauses (a)-(e): the corrected score coefficient, exact augmentation identities, expectation and variance, oracle bounds, normal limit and both conservative interval results. Interior truth and nondegeneracy concern the corrected variance, and the extra HAC homophily condition uses both node indices as required. Spatial integrability and positive finite masses guard ordinary circle averages; finite invertibility guards the displayed information inverse, and the asymptotic Gram hypothesis makes it eventually invertible. Independence is the explicit finite product Bernoulli law. General metric spaces and arbitrary finite tables specialize to all the claim's spatial settings. Representative nonsingular positive-probability finite premises and all finite identities were independently checked; an intercept-only logistic model has actual compact-set maximizers and interior truth. No contradictory or conclusion-assuming hypothesis was found.

Retains an actual constrained-MLE family with admissibility guards, eventual positivity of the actual fitted-estimator variance, and the printed-SAH/actual-variance ratio limit 8/25. The probability and denominator are the actual finite-design ones. The realization replaces the unit-disk outcome field by a counting-measure line table, and extends the 8r sequence to all sample sizes. W1-W3 formulas and numerical comparisons and the remaining W4 expansion, normal law, individual limits and coverage formula are absent. The two saturated groups have asymptotic proportions 1/4 and 3/4, probabilities 1/2 and 1/10, and bounded clipped actual MLEs, so the retained guards are jointly satisfiable; the N=32 variance and printed expectation were independently recomputed.

States both exact once-versus-twice weighting identities of (a), and the covariance-neighborhood bound and expected raw variance identity of (b), for arbitrary deterministic fits. It omits every numerical and asymptotic assertion in (c). The self and symmetry conditions describe the claim's neighborhoods and do not assume the bound. Positive propensities and, for the arm-denominator identities, positive arm counts exclude zero division. A two-node assignment with one node in each arm satisfies these premises; the identities and covariance bound were independently checked by exact enumeration on a five-node design.

Only Case B is asserted, with an actual binary Euclidean-area outcome field, the full all-assignment finite-table identity, positive bin areas, disjoint union, six-bin estimator and AME sums -17/500, and whole AME 121/18000. Cases A and C and grid refinement are absent. Distance to the closed unit disk gives precisely the stated successive annuli; the polar-angle sectors have the entered binary shares. The independently computed area-weighted mean has the claimed positive value. There is no assertion about an empirical application effect.

Retains the actual integral union identity, linearity for marginal means and node effects, node-average formula, range bounds, equal-mass formula, and positive-scale exceedance and p-value identities. The two negative assertions in (b), that an unweighted sum can leave the range and that bin AMEs need not identify the whole effect with node-specific masses, are not stated. Measurability, integrability, disjointness, positive finite bin masses and positive numbers of nodes/bins ensure that the normalized averages have their intended meaning; the area Case B and the finite positive-mass examples satisfy these premises. Arbitrary weights in the scaling identity harmlessly generalize the probability-weight case.

Retains the twenty-node finite reversal exactly, the repeated-star spatial/locality/homophily/nondegeneracy guards and exact linearized variance. The exact limiting coverage equality is replaced by an eventual upper bound at the same value, and the probability counts only draws with both arms nonempty and positive trace and trace-square parameters. Separate W1 spectral certificates, W2 moments, W3 variance/trace/ratio/degrees-of-freedom limits and Gaussian law are absent. The event is a joint event, not coverage conditional on validity. The star construction has no assignment-dependent outcomes and positive linearized variance; independent exact matrix calculations reproduce all finite constants and positive adjustment parameters on the displayed assignment.

Retains finite capped-PD ordering and interval inclusion and the asymptotic lower coverage bound for supplied critical values at least the normal quantile. It does not assert the universal Student-quantile comparison. The asymptotic event is an implication from nonempty arms, so empty-arm draws satisfy it; this is weaker than a coverage event that excludes invalid draws and is not conditional coverage. A supplied orthonormal spectral representation is required (every finite real symmetric uniform-distance kernel has one). Positive and negative spectral parts have the stated order; the cap divides by a number in (0,1] or leaves the variance unchanged. A fixed bounded heterogeneous no-interference line population supplies nondegeneracy and zero homophily, with nonempty-arm probability tending to one.

Retains the explicit actual boundary-constrained logistic maximizer, its complete LogisticConditions, the uniform 3/32 tail lower bound for every positive N, and failure of the score expansion. It omits the separately listed W1 numerical Gram/overlap certificates, W2 calculus/uniqueness, W3 information and negative-tail identities, W4 exact moments and sharper N-dependent bound, and the half-normal law. The piecewise definition correctly handles all-control/all-treated draws, so it is not a log-of-zero convention. The negative binomial tail yielding the lower bound was checked exactly for N=1 through 300. Boundary truth is allowed by the printed compact-membership condition and does not assume expansion failure.

States consistency and the root-N rate under compact membership, and both the order-N^-1 and little-o root-N score remainder conclusions under interior truth, matching (a)-(b). The finite product maximum norm is equivalent to the Euclidean norm in the fixed dimension and gives the same orders and consistency. The Gram lower bound is eventual, exactly the large-sample nonsingularity needed for these asymptotic conclusions. Compact likelihood maximizers exist; a positive-dimensional intercept model on the radius-one closed ball has actual maximizers, interior truth and overlap. Neither convexity nor the score expansion is smuggled into LogisticConditions.

States the corrected unbiasedness, the printed expectation, its exact equality criterion, and the constant-one/p=1/4 example for every positive sample size, exactly (a)-(c). The arbitrary finite table includes all well-defined spatial tables and does not constrain away interference. Only strict positivity of both arm probabilities is used, which is enough for these finite statements. The one-node example has corrected expectation zero, printed expectation -2 and positive variance 16/3; these were independently checked.

Retains the actual eight-node sharp-null spatial Witness A, exact draw-array probability 256^-101>0, printed proportion one, absolute exceedance count zero and plus-one p-value 1/101; and Witness B's exact rejection sum above 1/20. The universal negative-observation rule, signed-statistic size s/2, decimals and all of the seventeen-node P=10000 Witness C are absent. In B, mcExceedances applies absolute values, exactly implementing the permitted nonnegative statistic |HT|. The formula's natural subtractions are nonnegative on their finite ranges. Independent exact arithmetic gives size 0.05549969550171698 and a strictly positive rational excess over 1/20.

States all three corrected finite-sample claims, including arbitrary normalized nonnegative assignment weights, independent identical draws including the observed draw, weak absolute exceedances with ties, the two raw bounds, and the exact correction size. A statistic depending only on an assignment is the appropriate representation when the outcome field is fixed under the sharp null; absence of a redundant spatial null predicate does not change the result. There is no no-ties assumption. Weighted finite examples with and without ties independently satisfy every bound; a nontrivial normalized assignment law also has a direct Lean instance.

States only the actual atomic two-node Witness 2: finite positive shell measures, bounded outcomes, the two zero circle AMEs, disk and donut AMEs 1/6, and impossibility of every real weighted combination of the two circle AMEs equaling the donut effect. Witnesses 1 and 3 and the separate individual-node effects/shell-mass vectors are absent. Distances are exactly (4,5,5) and (5,4,4); all four averaging regions have positive counting mass, so no zero-area-circle convention is involved. Direct enumeration reproduces the effects.

Retains (a)'s point-effect integral and AME, an abstract finite-shell form of both identities in (b), (c)'s common-weight simplification on positive supported labels, and (d)'s exact normalized Euclidean annulus radial-measure density.
